newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot resids mixed again, HSFO still firm.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot resids mixed again, HSFO still firm.

text.p: U.S. spot fuel oil prices were mixed again Friday in thin trade, with firm bunkers still supporting high sulphur grades, while sluggish utility demand continued to plague low sulphur, industry sources said.

"The (cold) weather this week has helped the racks a little, but the (heating) season's over," said one cash trader, noting firm bunkers, particularly in the East were driving high sulphurs but utility demand remained slack.
In New York Harbor, traders again raised quotes for high sulphurs, with three percent up slightly to $14 a barrel or better and 2.2 percent rising to $14.25-50, traders said.

NYH 0.3 percent high pour remained well-offered but prompt prices were little changed in the $16.25 area. Traders said New York Power Authority on Monday may reissue its tender for 100,000 barrels of fairly prompt HP. NYPA rejected bids for a similar tender earlier this week.
NYH physical one percent eased slightly to $15.25, with May paper also down modestly to the low-$15 range.
At the U.S. Gulf, three percent notionally firmed slightly to $13.50, while one percent held at $15.00-25.
Traders said 50,000 barrels of prompt three percent sold Thursday at $13.35 (FOB Miss. River).

New York city gate weekend gas prices slipped a few cents Friday to the high-$2.30s/mmBtu, or $14.99 a barrel equivalent. Gas at Henry Hub, the NYMEX delivery point, firmed slightly to the high-$1.90s/mmBtu, or $12.47 a barrel.
